editorial:
Brideless Groom is a 1947 Three Stooges comedy short directed by Edward Bernds. Shemp plays a voice teacher who must marry before six o'clock to inherit a fortune, and nobody will accept his proposal. A short with this much circulation is an easy pick for a compilation, a classic-comedy channel or a remix.

The rights trap is that the film is the layer you can't yet call free. The Internet Archive tags one upload with a Public Domain Mark, but that is the uploader's claim. This dossier did not complete a search of the 1974–1976 Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes. Check the Stanford renewal database and those volumes yourself before relying on the film. Don't assume that a Public Domain Mark on one copy covers every version.
faq: Is Brideless Groom safe to reuse?

Not yet confirmed here. The Internet Archive tags one upload as public domain, but this dossier did not finish a renewal search. Search the Stanford renewal database and the 1974–1976 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes first.
Use a plain black-and-white upload and keep a record of the item page. Avoid any version with added material, such as colorization or new music, because those additions can carry their own copyright.
